# Multo (song)

"Multo" is a synth-pop and pop rock ballad by Filipino alternative pop band Cup of Joe . Released on September 14, 2024, as the first single from their debut album "Silakbo" , the song has achieved unprecedented success in the Philippine music industry, spending 27 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Philippines Hot 100 as of October 2025 . The song's title translates to "ghost" in English and explores themes of being haunted by unresolved emotions and memories .

## Background and release

"Multo" was written by Cup of Joe's lead vocalist Raphaell Ridao and his brother Redentor Immanuel Ridao during the COVID-19 lockdown restrictions . The song was born from Raphaell's personal experience of feeling "haunted" by unexplainable thoughts and emotions during the pandemic . "Naumpisahan namin 'yung song with the thought of some feeling, some people feel things na kahit ano'ng gawin mo, kahit pilit mong nilalayo, sumusunod sa'yo," Ridao recalled in an interview with GMA News .

The song was released as a surprise to fans on September 14, 2024, with the band announcing it just three hours before its scheduled release . It was produced by Shadiel Chan and released under Viva Records . The song marks a more introspective turn in the band's musical direction , departing from their usual upbeat pop sound to explore deeper emotional themes.

## Composition and lyrics

Musically, "Multo" is described as a synth-pop and pop rock ballad with melancholic elements . The song features ethereal melodies and hauntingly poignant lyrics . Rolling Stone Philippines' Elijah Pareño characterized it as a "sad banger" that disguises emotional collapse as a danceable moment .

The lyrics of "Multo" explore themes of longing, confusion, and the pain of unreciprocated feelings . The song uses the metaphor of a "ghost" to represent emotions and memories that persist even after one tries to move on. Key lyrics include "Ako ay dahan-dahang nililibing nang buhay pa" (I am being buried alive little by little) and "Minumulto na 'ko ng damdamin ko" (I am being haunted by my emotions) .

The song is part of Cup of Joe's concept album "Silakbo," which explores the five stages of grief . "Multo" specifically embodies the stage of denial, representing the "aching stillness" of refusing to accept loss .

## Reception and legacy

Since its release, "Multo" has achieved remarkable commercial success. The song first reached the No. 1 spot on the Billboard Philippines Hot 100 during the week of April 19, 2025, and has held that position for 27 consecutive weeks as of October 11, 2025 . This achievement makes it the longest-running No. 1 song in the chart's history .

The song has been streamed over 60 million times on Spotify and has 2.55 million daily streams . Cup of Joe has reached over 11.2 million monthly listeners on Spotify, making them the Filipino act with the most monthly listeners . "Multo" also topped Apple Music Philippines' Top OPM Songs of 2025 chart .

On social media, particularly TikTok, "Multo" has become a viral hit. The song's refrain "Binaon naman na ang lahat" (I have already buried everything) has become a trending audio clip . The song has been used as an unofficial love song for a popular PBB (Pinoy Big Brother) love team and has been featured in numerous edits involving K-drama breakups and other emotional content .

Critics have praised "Multo" for its poetic lyricism and cinematic soundscape, calling it a "signature blend of Cup of Joe's emotionally intelligent storytelling and genre-bending artistry" . The song has been described as "the soundtrack of every text you never sent" , resonating with listeners who find themselves dwelling on past relationships and unspoken emotions.

## International recognition

"Multo" has achieved historic milestones for Filipino music internationally. The song became the first Filipino song to enter the Top 40 of Billboard's Global Excl. US Chart, peaking at #33 . This achievement is considered a historic moment for Original Pilipino Music (OPM) .

The song's international success extends beyond chart performance. It has reached audiences in Southeast Asian countries and has been featured on international Spotify editorial playlists . This global reach has helped solidify Cup of Joe's position as ambassadors for OPM on the international stage.

## Music video

The music video for "Multo" features a beautifully minimalist aesthetic that complements the song's emotional tone. The video has garnered millions of views on YouTube and has been praised for its ability to enhance the song's haunting atmosphere through visual storytelling.

A stripped-down acoustic performance of "Multo" recorded at Cozy Cove has amassed over 3.3 million views . This performance, featuring raw vulnerability and minimal production, showcases the song's emotional core and the band's ability to deliver powerful performances without elaborate staging.

## Cultural impact

"Multo" has had a profound impact on Filipino popular culture. The song has been embraced as a representation of the collective experience of dealing with unresolved emotions and memories. Lead vocalist Gian Bernardino has emphasized that various interpretations of the song are valid, stating: "Dahil doon marami rin kaming natututunang perspective which inspires us, which motivates us. Kung ano man 'yung interpretation niyo ng 'Multo,' it's all valid" .

The song's success has also contributed to the resurgence of OPM in the global music scene. Keyboardist Xen Gareza attributes part of their international success to social media platforms, saying: "'Yung generation natin, we have the platform to reach international audiences so that's a big help and I believe na even then 'yung talent ng OPM talagang meron na" .

## Legacy

"Multo" has fundamentally altered Cup of Joe's artistic trajectory. The song represents the band's evolution from a group known for upbeat pop songs to serious pop storytellers unafraid to explore deep emotional themes . The lyrics "Pasindi na ng ilaw/ Minumulto na 'ko ng damdamin ko" (Turn on the light/I am being haunted by my emotions) have been interpreted as a metaphor for the band's own artistic journey, shedding their playful image to confront deeper emotional territories .

The song's success has also inspired other Filipino artists and has helped pave the way for increased international recognition of OPM. As Gian Bernardino stated: "Actually, long overdue na eh. OPM is very beautiful. It's very unique. It's something na could make waves internationally and I think it's time na rin kasi dati pa talaga dapat 'to" .

## Critical reception

Music critics have lauded "Multo" for its artistic merit and emotional depth. The song has been praised for its ability to balance infectious melodies with profound lyricism. Rolling Stone Philippines noted that the song "hits you straight in the feels as it delivers a poignant examination of the ghosts of our past, leaving one with a little more clarity on the ruins of their failed relationships" .

The song's minimalist approach to production has also been commended. Critics have highlighted how the stripped-back arrangement allows the emotional core of the song to shine through. The combination of Raphaell Ridao's emotive vocals and the song's haunting melody creates what many describe as a "mesmerizing" listening experience .

| Album | Silakbo (2025) |

## Charts performance

"Multo" has dominated music charts in the Philippines and achieved historic international milestones:

* **Billboard Philippines Hot 100**: 27 weeks at No. 1 (as of October 11, 2025)

* **Billboard Global Excl. US**: Peaked at No. 33 (first Filipino song to enter Top 40)

* **Spotify Philippines Top 50**: Charting position

* **Apple Music Philippines Top OPM Songs of 2025**: No. 1 

## Legacy and influence

"Multo" has established itself as a cultural touchstone in contemporary Filipino music. The song's ability to resonate with listeners across different age groups and backgrounds has made it an anthem for a generation navigating the complexities of modern relationships and emotions.

The song's success has also had a significant impact on the OPM industry. It has demonstrated that Filipino artists can create music that is both commercially successful and artistically meaningful. "Multo" has inspired a new wave of OPM artists to explore deeper emotional themes and has helped establish a new standard for Filipino popular music.

As Cup of Joe continues to build on the success of "Multo," the song remains a defining moment in their career and a landmark achievement for Filipino music. The band's lead vocalist Gian Bernardino has expressed gratitude for the song's success, stating: "Nakaka-proud, we're very thankful na part kami ng generation ng OPM na talagang nare-recognize internationally" .

### Luto e saudade persistem em "Multo" de Cup of Joe

O título "Multo", que significa "fantasma" em filipino, já indica o tema central da música do Cup of Joe: a presença emocional que permanece mesmo após o fim de um relacionamento ou a perda de alguém importante. A canção foi inspirada pelo luto vivido pelos irmãos Raphaell e Redentor Ridao durante a pandemia, o que se reflete em versos como “binaon naman na ang lahat / tinakpan naman na 'king sugat / ngunit ba't ba andito pa rin?” (já enterrei tudo / já cobri minha ferida / mas por que ainda está aqui?), mostrando a dificuldade de superar a dor e as lembranças que insistem em voltar.

A letra traz imagens claras de assombração emocional, como em “ako ay dahan-dahang nililibing nang buhay pa” (estou sendo enterrado vivo aos poucos) e “minumulto na 'ko ng damdamin ko, ng damdamin ko” (estou sendo assombrado pelos meus sentimentos, pelos meus sentimentos). Esses trechos deixam evidente que o "fantasma" não é só a lembrança de outra pessoa, mas também sentimentos não resolvidos. Expressões como “dinadalaw mo 'ko bawat gabi” (você me visita toda noite) e “haplos mo'y ramdam pa rin sa dilim” (ainda sinto seu toque no escuro) reforçam como a ausência se torna quase física, dificultando seguir em frente. Assim, "Multo" retrata de forma direta e sensível o peso do luto e da saudade, mostrando como memórias e emoções podem se tornar presenças constantes, mesmo quando parece que tudo já foi superado.

Billboard Philippines Honors Cup Of Joe For The Chart-Topping Success Of “Multo”
================================================================================

The achievement comes after the song has officially spent 27 weeks at No. 1 on the _Billboard Philippines_ Hot 100 as of the week of October 11, 2025.

By [Mayks Go](https://billboardphilippines.com/author/micah-go/ "Posts by Mayks Go")

October 13, 2025

[![Image 13: Facebook](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#facebook "Facebook")[![Image 14: X](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/x.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#x "X")[![Image 15: Telegram](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/telegram.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#telegram "Telegram")[![Image 16: Copy Link](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#copy_link "Copy Link")

![Image 17: SB19 receiving an award on stage, wearing black-and-red plaid coords](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CUP-OF-JOE-FTR-IMG-2-1600x838.jpg)

Cup of Joe: photographed by Mayks Go/Billboard Philippines

Cup of Joe: photographed by Mayks Go/Billboard Philippines

[Cup of Joe](https://billboardphilippines.com/tag/cup-of-joe/) and their biggest song yet, “Multo,” continue to showcase their widespread impact on Filipino listeners nationwide — a fact solidified by officially being the longest-reigning song on the _Billboard Philippines_ charts.

On October 12, 2025 (Sunday), the alternative pop band were presented by _Billboard Philippines_ publisher Anne Bernisca and managing editor Jason Caballa with a plaque of recognition for this feat. It was given to the band during the third day of their ‘Stardust’ Manila concert, held at the Smart Araneta Coliseum.

At the time of being given the award, “Multo” had held the No. 1 spot on the Philippines Hot 100 and Top Philippine Songs charts for 27 weeks straight — the most by any artist in the charts’ history. This achievement is significant as it not only objectively proves that “Multo” is currently the biggest song in the Philippines, but that it has also beaten out other viral and successful songs constantly being listened to by Filipino listeners in the past few months —including “Golden” from the _Kpop Demon Hunters_ soundtrack, NIKI’s cover of “You’ll Be In My Heart,” December Avenue’s “Saksi Ang Langit,” and more.

Advertisement

“Multo” first reached the No. 1 spot on the _Billboard Philippines_ charts during the week of April 19, 2025. Since then, it has held onto its position without contest.

Released on September 14, 2024, “Multo” is the first single from Cup of Joe’s debut album _Silakbo_, which came out on January 17, 2025. Since the song came out last year, it has seen a strong listenership nationwide, continuing to achieve millions of streams per week after initially going viral thanks to consistent usage on social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram.

Cup of Joe’s ‘Multo’ Is the Soundtrack of Every Text You Never Sent
===================================================================

A song that sounds like closure but feels like relapse, _Multo_ slips into your bloodstream—unwelcome, unforgettable, and impossibly true

By [Dayne Aduna](https://vman-sea.com/author/dayne-aduna/ "Posts by Dayne Aduna")

May 04, 2025

[![Image 5: Facebook](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://vman-sea.com/#facebook "Facebook")[![Image 6: Instagram](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/instagram.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fcup-of-joes-multo-is-the-soundtrack-of-every-text-you-never-sent%2F "Instagram")[![Image 7: X](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/x.svg)](https://vman-sea.com/#x "X")[![Image 8: Email](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/email.svg)](https://vman-sea.com/#email "Email")[![Image 9: Copy Link](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://vman-sea.com/#copy_link "Copy Link")

![Image 10: CUP OF JOE](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CUP-OF-JOE-PORTRAIT.webp?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

The anatomy of a haunting
-------------------------

In the late hours when memory sharpens and silence stretches, Filipino pop/rock band [Cup of Joe](https://www.instagram.com/cupofjoemusic_/?hl=en)’s _Multo_ begins to echo—not just through headphones, but across the tender, private landscapes of broken hearts and unfinished stories. Released with almost no warning on a Friday night, the song arrived like a whisper from the past, unannounced yet eerily familiar, as if it had been waiting for us to feel just fragile enough to let it in.

_[Multo](https://open.spotify.com/track/4cBm8rv2B5BJWU2pDaHVbF)_, which translates to “ghost” in Filipino, is neither a ballad of heartbreak nor a love song in its traditional sense. Instead, it is a haunting—a sonic visitation from the unresolved and the almosts, a reckoning with the echoes of relationships that end but never quite exit. It’s the slow, involuntary re-opening of doors you once slammed shut, the return to digital ruins—old conversations, unsent drafts, photos you thought you’d deleted. With its infectious rhythm and confessional lyricism, _Multo_ disguises emotional collapse as a danceable moment, a pop exorcism where you sway through the ache instead of succumbing to it.

![Image 11: CUP OF JOE](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/CUP-OF-JOE-BANNER.webp?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

But perhaps the most disarming part of _Multo_ is its emotional clarity. The track doesn’t beg for reconciliation; it documents the relapse. One that doesn’t announce itself in grand gestures but in relapses: checking if they’ve seen your story, listening to the voice note one more time, wondering if, under new circumstances, old love could survive.

Advertisement

Scenery as sentiment
--------------------

The song is a continuation of Cup of Joe’s lyrical ethos—poetry disguised as pop, heartbreak rendered in imagery so specific it becomes collective. _Multo_ joins a lineage of works like _Tingin_, _Patutunguhan_, and _Nag-iisang Muli_, where location and emotion are fused into landscapes of longing, often borrowing the chill and mist of their hometown Baguio to frame emotional weather.

Where _Patutunguhan_ navigated tides and _Tingin_ looked through the filtered lens of a distant gaze, _Multo_ simply lingers. It doesn’t move forward. It circles. Like the ghosts it names, it returns to the same emotional hallway, dragging its metaphorical chains through the listener’s already cracked foundation. And yet, it doesn’t feel oppressive—it feels true. There’s an honesty in its repetition, a comfort in the ache.

It’s this authenticity that has made the track viral. On TikTok, _Multo_ is the unofficial theme of digital mourning. Edits splice it with K-drama breakups, celebrity love team throwbacks, even anonymous videos of fingers hovering over “send” buttons. It’s no longer just a song; it’s a ritual. In a world where vulnerability is currency and collective grief is algorithmic gold, the song gives voice to a generation fluent in emotional residue.

Advertisement

A band that keeps evolving
--------------------------

And yet, for all its pain, the song is not hopeless. There’s no promise of reunion, but there is the suggestion of reckoning. To name a ghost is to begin to release it. In that sense, _Multo_ is about being haunted and becoming aware of the haunting—and perhaps, in time, learning how to live beside it.

Cup of Joe’s rise in the Filipino music scene has been nothing short of remarkable. With over four million monthly listeners and a string of charting singles, they’ve become the rare act that transcends trend. Their music has become a mirror to youth culture—specifically, its oscillation between sincerity and sarcasm, its reliance on nostalgia as both balm and burden.

In songs like _Misteryoso_ and _Lahat ng Bukas_, the band has mapped out entire emotional ecosystems. Their first EP _Patutunguhan_ was a testament to their range, featuring collaborations that expanded their sound without diluting their identity. Now, with _Multo_, they’ve found their pulse point: the devastation that lives beneath even the brightest melodies.

Advertisement

Cup of Joe’s success lies not just in their sound, but in their understanding of silence—what is left unsaid, what remains undone. Their music doesn’t offer resolution. It offers reflection. And in _Multo_, they have distilled that reflection into its most potent form: a ghost that doesn’t scare, but simply stays.

Cup Of Joe Summon The Ghosts Of Their Past On New Single “Multo” – Listen
=========================================================================

This marks their latest release since dropping the chart-topping “Misteryoso.”

By [Gabriel Saulog](https://billboardphilippines.com/author/gabriel-saulog/ "Posts by Gabriel Saulog")

September 16, 2024

[![Image 13: Facebook](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#facebook "Facebook")[![Image 14: X](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/x.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#x "X")[![Image 15: Telegram](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/telegram.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#telegram "Telegram")[![Image 16: Copy Link](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/themes/billboardph/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://billboardphilippines.com/#copy_link "Copy Link")

![Image 17: A Filipino boy band, composed of five stylish men, are posing in front of a yellow background, with 2 men standing on top of the other 3 seated on a chair](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/cup-of-joe-ftr-img-fixed-1600x838.jpg)

Courtesy of @cupofm

Cup of Joe: courtesy of @cupofjoemusic.

[Cup Of Joe](https://billboardphilippines.com/music/news/cup-of-joe-announce-dos-the-sixth-joenniversary-special-concert-tickets-2024/ "Cup of Joe Announce ‘DOS: The Sixth JOEnniversary Special’") are here to haunt your ears for the better with their new single, titled “Multo.”

The new track came as a surprise release to their Joe-wahs and other fans last September 13, 2024 (Friday), as the group announced the track a mere three hours before its scheduled release.

Yet as many of their listeners have discovered, “Multo” hits you straight in the feels as it delivers a poignant examination of the ghosts of our past, leaving one with a little more clarity on the ruins of their failed relationships. Even sonically, the track itself is a bit more ambitious and experimental for the band, with a hook that lingers deep upon its first full listen.

”Multo” marks the latest entry in Cup Of Joe’s discography, and follows the release of their chart-topping single “Misteryoso” and “Lahat Ng Bukas,” featuring Keanna Mag. The group also released their first ever extended play (EP) _Patutunguhan_ late last year, which includes the hit single “Tingin” with Janine Teñoso.

Advertisement

Both “Tingin” and “Misteryoso” are currently charting on the _Billboard Philippines_ Hot 100 with their other single “Estranghero.” “Tingin” stands at No. 12, “Misteryoso” at No. 28, and “Estranghero” at No. 69. Together with many other chart-topping musicians, Cup Of Joe are set to take the grand stage for _Billboard Philippines_’ first-anniversary event, [_Mainstage_](https://billboardphilippines.com/music/how-to-secure-your-spot-at-billboard-philippines-mainstage-the-year-one-anniversary/ "How to Secure Your Spot at Billboard Philippines: Mainstage – The Year One Anniversary"), this October 15, 2024. Tickets to the show may be purchased [here](https://billboardphilippines.com/music/how-to-secure-your-spot-at-billboard-philippines-mainstage-the-year-one-anniversary/ "How to Secure Your Spot at Billboard Philippines: Mainstage – The Year One Anniversary").

How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

CMP privacy choices

Storage, duration, and usage details
------------------------------------

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
*   For **sites**, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
*   For **apps**, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
*   For **accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites**, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.

6.title: Cup of Joe’s “Multo” haunts the charts with its mesmerizing success | Pikapika | Philippine Showbiz News Portal
6.description: With over 11.2 million monthly listeners on Spotify, Cup of Joe is currently the most listened-to OPM band on the platform—even breaking the long-held streak of an international artist to become the longest-running #1 Artist on Spotify Philippine...
6.content:
[![Image 1: Since its release, “Multo” has become a viral hit, charting on Spotify Philippines’ Top 50 and earning a spot on multiple editorial playlists like Tatak Pinoy and OPM Rising. Fans have also flooded TikTok with personal renditions and interpretations of the song, with the haunting refrain “Binaon naman na ang lahat” becoming a trending audio clip.](https://www.pikapika.ph/storage/media/image/article/caeed832ab664f42bc7ebe8a0ea0edc6/images/6a80fc96f3a1c64dedea0fbac9f3b9fe/conversions/Untitled-design-(15)-feature.jpg?v=1747904962)](https://www.pikapika.ph/storage/media/image/article/caeed832ab664f42bc7ebe8a0ea0edc6/images/6a80fc96f3a1c64dedea0fbac9f3b9fe/Untitled-design-(15).jpg?v=1747904962)

PHOTO: Viva Records

Since its release, “Multo” has become a viral hit, charting on Spotify Philippines’ Top 50 and earning a spot on multiple editorial playlists like Tatak Pinoy and OPM Rising. Fans have also flooded TikTok with personal renditions and interpretations of the song, with the haunting refrain “Binaon naman na ang lahat” becoming a trending audio clip.

With over 11.2 million monthly listeners on Spotify, [Cup of Joe](https://www.pikapika.ph/pikadaily/exclusive-cup-of-joe-on-virality-of-hit-song-multo-na-encapsulate-niya-yong-yearning-for-things-that-could-have-been) is currently the most listened-to OPM band on the platform—even breaking the long-held streak of an international artist to become the longest-running #1 Artist on Spotify Philippines.

OPM sensation Cup of Joe proves once again that they’re a force to be reckoned with as their emotionally-charged single “Multo” continues to captivate listeners and dominate streaming charts across the country.

Tumuklas pa

celeb

Celebrity

A standout track from their concept album Silakbo—which explores the five stages of grief—“Multo”embodies the aching stillness of denial, cloaked in ethereal melodies and hauntingly poignant lyrics. The song’s title, meaning “ghost” in Filipino, becomes a powerful metaphor for the people and feelings we can’t seem to let go of, no matter how much time has passed.

**RELATED:[EXCLUSIVE! Cup of Joe on virality of hit song Multo: “Na-encapsulate niya ‘yong yearning for things that could have been.”](https://www.pikapika.ph/pikadaily/exclusive-cup-of-joe-on-virality-of-hit-song-multo-na-encapsulate-niya-yong-yearning-for-things-that-could-have-been)**

Since its release, “Multo” has become a viral hit, charting on Spotify Philippines’ Top 50 and earning a spot on multiple editorial playlists like Tatak Pinoy and OPM Rising. Fans have also flooded TikTok with personal renditions and interpretations of the song, with the haunting refrain “Binaon naman na ang lahat” becoming a trending audio clip.

[![Image 2: A Filipino band, Multo, is recognized as the first Filipino act to break into the Billboard Global 200](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%201.jpeg)](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%201.jpeg)

Critics have praised “Multo” for its poetic lyricism and cinematic soundscape, a signature blend of Cup of Joe’s emotionally intelligent storytelling and genre-bending artistry. Paired with a beautifully minimalist music video that has already garnered millions of views on YouTube, the track continues to resonate deeply with listeners navigating heartbreak, memory, and loss.

[![Image 3: Group of 5 music artists in red toned filter, and text indicates the group's rank on Spotify top songs and artists](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%202.jpeg)](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%202.jpeg)

“Multo" also reached audiences in Southeast Asian countries and broke into international Spotify editorial playlists, a testament to the band’s growing global resonance. Most notably, it became the first Filipino song to reach the Top 40 of Billboard’s Global Excl. US Chart, peaking at #33—a historic moment for OPM. On Spotify Philippines, "Multo" currently holds the #1 spot with 1.599 million streams, continuing its reign on the platform.

[![Image 4: Group photo of a band on a red background with the number 1 at the top, and the phrase 'on spotify top artists chart'](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%203.jpg)](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%203.jpg)

“This is one of our most vulnerable songs,” shared the band in a recent interview. “Multo came from a place of still holding on—even when you know you shouldn't. We wanted to honor that very human experience.”

[![Image 5: The music band “Multo” tops both the Spotify PH chart and Apple Music PH chart](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%204.jpg)](https://www.pikapika.ph/ckeditor/photos/26/1%20PPOP/MILESTONE%204.jpg)

With "Multo," Cup of Joe solidifies their place not just as hitmakers, but as storytellers unafraid to go deep. As the ghostly echoes of the track continue to ripple through airwaves and hearts alike, it’s safe to say: this song is here to haunt us—in the best way possible.

The making of 'Multo' and the rise of OPM band Cup Of Joe to global success
===========================================================================

 By JOSIAH ANTONIO

**Published** May 1, 2025 10:20am 

![Image 10: The making of 'Multo' and the rise of OPM band Cup Of Joe to global success](https://images.gmanews.tv/webpics/2025/05/gnarly_(14)_2025_05_01_10_19_47.jpg)

Locked in the four walls of their house during the lockdown restrictions, Cup of Joe lead vocalist Rapha Ridao and his brother, Red, poured out their emotions and gave birth to the hit song "Multo."

ADVERTISEMENT

Little did they know that the song will come crashing into the [Billboard Global 200 charts](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942862/cup-of-joe-multo-billboard-global-200/story/) five years later and help catapult the band into a different level of success.

"Kaming dalawa (ng kuya ko) 'yung nagsulat nung pandemic kasi nung time na 'yung 'di kami makalabas, wala kaming ibang (alam) gawin. It gave us time to reflect din kasi there's no escape nung (time) na 'yun eh," Ridao told GMA News in an interview.

Released in 2024, "Multo" has since fetched more than 60 million streams on Spotify. It's become so popular on TikTok, and has been used as an unofficial love song for popular [PBB love team](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942027/cup-of-joe-gian-bernardino-will-ashley-bianca-de-vera/story/)Will Ashley and Bianca de Vera.

With listeners having different interpretations and entries to the viral hit, Cup of Joe discussed the meaning behind the song and how important it is to them to raise the flag of OPM after the song's success.

**Shadows of the Past**

In 2020, Rapha was feeling a lot of things with the pandemic and felt like something was holding him back.

"Naumpisahan namin 'yung song with the thought of some feeling, some people feel things na kahit ano'ng gawin mo, kahit pilit mong nilalayo, sumusunod sa'yo," he recalled.

With the idea of someone following a person, the singer thought of a ghost or "multo" in Filipino and worked on the song with the said word.

"Napunta sa 'min 'yung thought na what if we use 'yung 'multo' as a figure na sinusundan ka. 'Yung feeling na 'yun, 'yung medyo scary," he said.

For Rapha, he wanted the listeners to feel how it's like to be haunted by your unexplainable thoughts and the past like a ghost.

"Gusto naming mapadama sa kanila 'yung element of being haunted. 'Yung feeling na parang wala ka namang nakikita pero andun pa rin eh, andun 'yung bigat. 'Yung mga emotions that can't be explained naturally 'yung mga ganoon," he said.

With the idea of making their album, "Multo" also helped Cup of Joe to circle around the five stages of grief with their album "Silakbo" released in January.

While the song quickly gained traction, processing its success was slow and enduring.

“Actually na-feel lang namin nung time na nagpahinga kami, nag-break from gigs tas doon namin nakikita na ‘ito na pala ‘yun’ ‘yung song na ‘to, No. 1 na,” said Gab Fernandez.

“Hindi namin siya ma-feel nang maayos kasi hindi kami magkakasama pero parang nung nagkasama-sama na kami parang doon lang namin na-feel ‘yung success namin,” he added.

Lead vocalist Gian Bernardino was glad with the reception of the song stressing how the varying interpretations of people with the song are valid.

"It goes along with the other songs na ni-release namin. We created the song with an initial thought then we shared it with the world then they came off with a different perspective and interpretation of the song," the singer said.

"Dahil doon marami rin kaming natututunang perspective which inspires us, which motivates us. Kung ano man 'yung interpretation niyo ng 'Multo,' it's all valid," he added.

**Long Overdue**

Recently reaching 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify — the most for a Filipino act — Cup of Joe stands among the likes of equally successful OPM acts like Juan Karlos, BINI, and Earl Agustin. Gian is just proud to be in the elite cadre.

“Nakaka-proud, we're very thankful na part kami ng generation ng OPM na talagang nare-recognize internationally,” he said.

Keyboardist Xen Gareza is quick to point to social media in helping them reach a wider audience, saying "'yung generation natin, we have the platform to reach international audiences so that's a big help and I believe na even then 'yung talent ng OPM talagang meron na."

“It's only now that we have the platform to go global or to reach further audiences na nare-recognize na rin nila 'yung skills ng Filipinos making art, music,” he added.

Gian stressed how it’s “long overdue” for more OPM acts to gain recognition internationally and it’s time for more artists to join them.

“Actually, long overdue na eh. OPM is very beautiful. It's very unique. It's something na could make waves internationally and I think it's time na rin kasi dati pa talaga dapat 'to. We're glad na we're part of that movement or mechanism na nag-start ng pagkilala ng mundo sa OPM,” he said.

Rafa and CJ Fernandez thanked their supporters and stressed how they made their success possible.

“Thank you kasi ever since 'yung support niyo ramdam na ramdam namin dito (sa puso) ... We're gonna make you guys happy and show you the love na pinapakita niyo sa amin,” Rafa said.

“Sobrang excited namin sa mga following months pa para sa lahat ng mangyayari kaya ayun sana abangan niyo,” CJ added.

Right now, Gian said that they are in the works of introducing more of the other songs in the “Silakbo” album to their listeners noting how there’s more to show with the tracks.

“Gusto lang namin sabihin, you're gonna like this, you've been waiting for this pero in terms of our music, we still have the whole year to introduce the whole album to, not only the Philippines but to the whole world, kasi there's more to see, to hear, to know about the 'Silakbo' album,” he said.

That, and relishing the moment's success.

"As a band we're very much immersing ourselves at the moment, kumbaga, we're living the moment. We're not really pressuring ourselves to achieve greater heights at where we are right now,” the lead vocalist said.

“As much as possible, we do our best every time and bonus na lang kung ano 'yung magiging reception ng tao,” he added. **— LA, GMA Integrated News**
